_comment: The VALUE FIELD, Layer A of the decision-substrate roadmap (owner-ordered keystone; docs/LAYERS_RESEARCH.md), and its move-intent consumer, env-gated SWEG_VALUE_MOVE, default OFF, byte-identical when unset. This is an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC, NOT a Warhammer 40,000 10th-edition game rule — there is no codex or core rule that tells a player which objective marker to move toward. Following the precedent of simulator.target_economics and simulator.threat_projection_charge (both explicitly-flagged AI design heuristics), this entry quotes the core primary-scoring wording (control the objective marker to score) and the wound-roll-and-save wording the field's survival math is built from, and cites the real-play multi-round mission-management doctrine that motivates it: a competent player values a position by what holding it is worth over the ROUNDS THAT REMAIN, discounted by the chance the unit standing there survives to score, and declines a marker whose realised yield is below the exposure it costs. THE GAP this layer closes: every AI decision in the sim was LOCAL and SINGLE-TURN — no unit reasoned about the scoring rounds ahead (pick_army_plan was a five-string proxy; the move planner scored objectives by a flat distance-weighted steal/capture heuristic with no horizon and no survival discount). The value field is the missing multi-round horizon: the dual of the threat field. The mechanic does not change combat math or draw any new random number — it only re-points the move planner's argmax among already-legal objective destinations toward the marker whose multi-round value net of exposure is highest, and it never freezes a claim or contest (it re-routes only).

simulator.value_projection.rule_name: Primary Mission scoring (control objective markers each battle round) + Wound roll (Strength vs Toughness) and Saving throw / invulnerable save (10e Core Rules) — multi-round objective-value piloting heuristic
simulator.value_projection.quoted_text: At the end of each Command phase, starting from the second battle round, the player whose turn is taking place scores 5 victory points for each objective marker they control (to a maximum of 15 victory points). A player controls an objective marker if they have a greater Objective Control characteristic total of models within range of it than their opponent. ... for each of those attacks that successfully wounded the target unit, the player commanding that unit can attempt a saving throw ... if that unit has an invulnerable save, the player can use that instead of their normal saving throw.
simulator.value_projection.trigger: SWEG_VALUE_MOVE=1 (default off, byte-identical when unset). In strategy.py pick_move_intent, for each candidate objective destination, compute the value field V(p) = marker_vp * control * contestability + secondary_positional_value, where marker_vp = obj.vp_per_round * scoring_rounds_remaining (rounds remaining read from the battle-round counter, MAX_ROUNDS = 5, current round inclusive, monotone non-increasing); control is 1.0 when the unit's PROSPECTIVE Objective Control at the marker (its own OC added to friendly OC already there) exceeds the enemy's, 0.5 on a tie (deny), 0.2 when it would still lose the count; contestability = 1 - frac_at_risk with frac_at_risk = min(1, T(marker centre) / the unit's remaining wounds); T(p) is the incoming threat field summed over every LIVING enemy via strategy._threat_field_at, reusing the cached threat-field projectors (strategy._threat_projectors) and the same audited expected-wounds per-pair math (simulator._ranged_expected_wounds attenuated by the positional Benefit-of-Cover tax; strategy._kill_potential_wounds times the real 2D6 charge-reach probability) that simulator.threat_projection_charge already uses; and secondary_positional_value adds a modest per-remaining-round value when the army's ALREADY-PICKED secondaries (army.chosen_secondaries from strategy.pick_secondaries) include Behind Enemy Lines and the destination is inside the enemy deployment zone. No new random number is drawn. SWEG_VALUE_MOVE_FACTIONS (per-faction piloting scope, second layer on this same consumer, added after the global-on screen moved five under-poles — Astra Militarum, Death Guard, Imperial Knights, Chaos Knights, World Eaters — decisively toward real but regressed five calibrated factions): an optional comma-separated allow-list of exact faction names (unit.profile.faction / evaluate_vs_meta.py FACTIONS strings, whitespace stripped per name). Read every pick_move_intent call, same as SWEG_VALUE_MOVE itself. When set and non-empty, `_use_value_move` is forced False for any unit whose faction is not in the list, so that unit's destination pick falls through to the legacy distance-weighted argmax exactly as if SWEG_VALUE_MOVE were unset for it (and SWEG_TRADE_EVAL's tilt, which only composes when the value gate is acted upon, is likewise inert for it); units whose faction IS in the list are unaffected and still consult the value field as described above. Unset or empty preserves the current all-factions behaviour, byte-identical to the v1 gate. Introduces no new random number and does not touch SWEG_VALUE_MOVE_DIAG's shadow counters, which remain a global measurement instrument. SWEG_VALUE_OFFENSE (offense rider on this same consumer, default off, byte-identical when unset; composes only when SWEG_VALUE_MOVE is acting for the unit) closes a measured defect: the value field priced a destination's marker worth and body exposure but its OWN damage output at zero, so a unit walking to a marker surrendered its firing position for free. When set, it adds to each candidate destination's net score the OUTPUT value of the cell — for each living enemy reachable from the candidate cell, the moving unit's expected wounds dealt me-to-enemy (the audited simulator._ranged_expected_wounds and strategy._kill_potential_wounds helpers, the same per-pair math the threat field uses enemy-to-me, here reversed) are capped at that enemy's remaining wounds and converted to victory points with the SAME exchange rate the trade evaluator uses (strategy._trade_vp_per_wound: the target's points-per-wound times the value field's relevance (5 * scoring_rounds_remaining) / 175); the offense is the BEST single reachable target's converted value, mirroring the trade evaluator's one-target commitment (a unit commits to one target next activation) — the earlier sum-over-reachable-targets form was repriced after screening showed it over-credits high-volume multi-target platforms into central coverage cells. The horizon discount is inherited through that relevance factor (linear in scoring_rounds_remaining, exactly as marker_vp scales) and the geometry mirrors strategy._threat_field_at in reverse (weapon-range reach, the same _cover_attenuation Benefit-of-Cover save tax applied to the target at its own cell against the mover's armour penetration, and the real 2D6 melee-reach gradient). Output is conditioned on the move class the resolution engine actually enforces, not the rulebook classes: a stationary candidate (a marker the unit already holds) prices full output including the Heavy keyword's +1 to Hit; a Normal-Move candidate prices output without the Heavy bonus; an Advance-required candidate prices ranged output only under a shoot-after-advance exemption and melee only under an advance-charge exemption, mirroring the exact gates in simulator._do_shoot and simulator._do_charge (profile.assault / transient_assault_this_round / Mont'ka Killing Blow rounds 1-3 / Bold Gallantry / Relentless Onslaught / Bringers of Flame / Gladius Devastator Doctrine / Star Engines for shooting; Gladius Assault Doctrine / murderers_cowl / transient_charge_after_advance for charging), reading only state present at move-decision time (transient stratagem flags are set by the round-start dispatch strictly before the movement phase, so they are visible; nothing is speculated). No new random number is drawn and no new tunable constant is introduced. SWEG_VALUE_OFFENSE_DIAG is its gate-off shadow counter (offense re-route rate and Heavy-weapon-unit hold-rate), a measurement instrument only.
simulator.value_projection.effect: AI move-intent destination-selection heuristic (Layer A consumer 2). The move planner's legacy distance-weighted objective argmax is replaced by the value-field net score net(p) = V(p) - unit_future_value * frac_at_risk(p), where unit_future_value = 5 * scoring_rounds_remaining is the unit's own remaining victory-point worth (its per-unit dual, consolidating the resource/attrition budget of Layer E) and frac_at_risk is the fraction of that value forfeited by exposing the body at p (from the threat field). Job value and body exposure are priced together (the threat-tolerance composition of docs/THREAT_LAYER_PROPOSAL.md): a marker worth several rounds of primary that the unit can survive to hold outscores a nearer marker in a kill zone, while a fragile unit likely to die before it scores discounts that marker's value — the durability differentiation is EMERGENT from T/remaining-wounds (tiny for a big wound pool, large for chaff), with no per-faction knob. The mission-override rule is preserved: the consumer only RE-ROUTES among claim/contest destinations (the legacy tuple, intent and score, flows downstream unchanged, so every intent, threshold and cover-snap below is identical); it never freezes a claim or contest into a hold, and the genuine marginal-holder hold-check runs earlier and is untouched. This is an AI design heuristic, not a 10e rule — the quoted primary-scoring, wound-roll and saving-throw wording is the scoring and combat math the value and survival figures are built from; it alters no dice, roll, or damage value. Faithful and even-handed: it fires for ALL factions and prices ANY marker for ANY moving unit; both armies consult it (the substrate escape from the closed-matrix wash). The OFF path leaves the legacy objective argmax byte-identical, validated by a common-random-number event-stream match against the base anchor. HONEST CAVEAT (per the proposal): the ranged half of T is attenuated only by the angle-independent positional cover the sim's shooting RESOLUTION enforces, not line-of-sight occlusion — the field plans with the geometry the resolution applies; the planned-kill discount (reducing T by fire this turn is about to allocate) is deferred because fire-allocation state is not cleanly readable at move time (documented in docs/THREAT_LAYER_PROPOSAL.md as consumer-2 work), and Engage on All Fronts is not priced per destination because it is a whole-army table-spread condition the machinery does not expose cheaply at one cell.

_value_field_doctrine_reference: Real-play doctrine motivating this heuristic, presented as doctrine (not a rules citation) per the same disclosure pattern as the _target_priority_doctrine_reference note in data/rule_citations.d/target_economics.json and the _threat_range_doctrine_reference note in data/rule_citations.d/threat_layer.json: competitive 10th-edition play is explicitly multi-round value management — in the pre-game you identify which units you want alive in the late game and protect them so they can shift the Primary to you in the later rounds, and you play the mission over the whole game rather than the local firefight. Sources: https://grimhammertactics.com/40k-tactics-how-to-build-a-gameplan-for-competitive-40k-missions/ (build a gameplan: protect the units that will hold the objectives in the scoring rounds) and https://www.goonhammer.com/start-competing-your-guide-to-getting-better-at-warhammer-40000/ (play the mission across the whole game), both already cited elsewhere in this project for the same multi-round mission-management doctrine. NOTE (honesty about verification): consistent with the notes recorded for simulator.target_economics and simulator.threat_projection_charge in this codebase, the Goonhammer / Grimhammer pages are JavaScript-rendered and their exact live text could not be re-confirmed by WebFetch this session; the multi-round value-management concept paraphrased here is the standard real-play doctrine the docs/LAYERS_RESEARCH.md design research and the researched playbooks already cite, and that document records it as the mechanism this layer models.
